# PREFIX-876 — Sparse two-toggle lattice collision lifting and exact 3:1 exclusion union

Date: 2026-11-17. Scope: independent portable auxiliary named-binary BRC observer research, extending PREFIX-874 and PREFIX-875. Frozen scientific-input pin remains \`f42f2906d77f24085c123f3ccfe9667d41caa96d\`. Research provenance: current scheduled R6 continuation; historical registered researcher EM-DIRECT-66B43A / session MCP-fd0fa1850d90423180438ef799a4c632; no newly acquired shared X6 CLAIM. Status: AUTHOR_PROVED / EXACT_INTEGER_CERTIFICATE / NOT_INDEPENDENTLY_REVIEWED / NOT_ADMITTED.

## Exact problem and model

Fix p named binary sources, N=2^p, and legal ordered events E_p={(u,u)} union {(u,u XOR 2^i):0<=u<N,0<=i<p}. Two predetermined odd moduli observe Phi(u,v)=(u mod q1,v mod q2). We require injectivity on all E_p, retaining source index, event direction, unchanged events and ordered old/new states. This is an *auxiliary* BRC observation model. It is not a native X6 Cell/Link/Port embedding or an additional spatial axis.

PREFIX-874 gave a constructive collision for the near-diagonal condition |q1-q2| in the sparse family D_B. PREFIX-875 lifted a one-power difference to kq1-lq2=2^i. The present result lifts the *entire sparse family* to arbitrary positive multiples and counts a new p=32 family exactly, without iterating over all 68,719,476,736 pairs.

## Theorem 876-A: sparse short-lattice collision lifting

Let p>=1, q1,q2,k,l be positive integers and a=kq1, b=lq2. Suppose a>b, d=a-b belongs to one of the following three families with available distinct bit indices:

(I) d=2^i, 0<=i<p;
(II) d=2^i+2^j, 0<=j<i<p;
(III) d=2^i-2^j, 0<=j<i<p.

Assume max(a,b)+2^(i+2)<N. Then Phi is noninjective on the complete ordered legal event set. The conclusion also applies with the two port orders reversed by time-reversal symmetry.

Proof: In each case put z=2^i, t=2^j where applicable, and construct the two distinct legal events A=(u,v), C=(u+a,v+b):

(I) Take u=0 when bit_i(a)=1, otherwise u=z; let A=(u,u) and C=(u+a,u+b)=(u+a,u+a-z). Then C flips bit i down, since bit_i(u+a)=1.

(II) Choose u exactly as in (I). Since j<i, bit_j(u)=0. Put A=(u,u+t), C=(u+a,u+b+t)=(u+a,u+a-z). These are respectively an upward j-flip and a downward i-flip.

(III) Let u=t if bit_i(a+t)=1, otherwise u=t+z. Then bit_j(u)=1 and bit_i(u+a)=1. Put A=(u,u-t), C=(u+a,u+b-t)=(u+a,u+a-z). Both are legal downward single-bit flips, of the distinct named bits j and i.

For all three cases u<2^(i+1), and any displayed old/new integer is nonnegative and smaller than max(a,b)+2^(i+2)<N. First coordinates differ by kq1 and second coordinates by lq2, so the observations match. The old states differ by a>0, proving a collision. Time reversal exchanges the two moduli while maintaining legal events. QED.

The theorem only needs the stated source-range/slack hypotheses; positivity of k,l is an explicit hypothesis. It does not claim a two-bit update within an event: each of the two *compared* events changes at most one named source.

## Theorem 876-B: exact new 3:1 family for p=32, B=19

Put Q=2^19-1=524287, N=2^32, and let D_19 be PREFIX-874's distinct 307-element set:
D_19 = {2^i:1<=i<19} union {2^i+2^j:1<=j<i<19} union {2^i-2^j:1<=j<i<=19}.
Extend it by two values, D*=D_19 union {2^19,2^20}, so |D*|=309.

For each positive odd q1,q2<=Q with 3q1-q2 in D*, Theorem 876-A applies with k=3,l=1. Indeed every required bit index is at most 20; a=3q1<=3Q, so max(a,b)+2^22<=3(2^19-1)+2^22<2^32. Every such pair, including the diagonal case, has an explicit collision.

The number of all such *ordered* pairs, including diagonals, is **27,000,811**. Exactly 34 are diagonal; hence 27,000,777 are non-diagonal. The intersection of the non-diagonal family with PREFIX-874's near-diagonal set |q1-q2| in D_19 consists of exactly **25,427** pairs. Therefore the 3:1 sparse-lattice family contributes **26,975,350** non-diagonal exclusions beyond PREFIX-874.

The previous PREFIX-875 non-diagonal 3:1 power family is a subset of the present family: it has 1,747,629 pairs, of which 1,746,491 are outside PREFIX-874. Consequently the *strict increment* in distinct excluded pairs over the union of PREFIX-874 and PREFIX-875 is **25,228,859**. The confirmed three-family union is:

    136,052,720 + 26,975,350 = 163,028,070

distinct ordered positive-odd modulus pairs in the B=19 square. This is an exact count for the specified collision-certificate union, not an exhaustive exclusion of all moduli. The p=32 optimal-width boundary remains B_fix,odd(32) in {19,20}.

### Exact finite counting proof

For a fixed d in D*, the relation q2=3q1-d and both 1<=q1,q2<=Q is equivalent to q1 odd in the closed integer interval

    L_d=max(1,ceil((d+1)/3)),
    U_d=min(Q,floor((Q+d)/3)).

The count of odd integers in [L_d,U_d] is max(0,floor((U_d-L'_d)/2)+1), where L'_d is the least odd integer >=L_d. Distinct d produce disjoint families because d=3q1-q2 is determined by the pair. Summing this exact expression over all 309 values gives 27,000,811. The diagonal criterion is d=2q1 with q1 odd, yielding exactly 34.

For the intersection with PREFIX-874, write q2=q1+s h, where h in D_19 and s in {-1,+1}. Then d=2q1-s h, so q1=(d+s h)/2. Checking this explicitly determined candidate for each (d,h,s) against the odd-modulus interval and endpoints is *complete*: all 309*307*2 triples are considered; no collision witness sampling is used to derive the count. The exact result is 25,427. The old PREFIX-875 outside-near count 1,746,491 is recovered independently by restricting d=2^i, 1<=i<=20.

## Computation, evidence and reusable method

The exact Python reference program PREFIX876_R6_SPARSE_LATTICE_3TO1_CHECK.py constructs each sparse representation, applies the closed arithmetic interval count, computes the complete sparse/near-diagonal intersection, checks explicit legal XOR transitions at low/high/interior parameter representatives for every d, and compares closed counts against a direct double-loop enumeration for small B=3,4,5,6. It produces PREFIX876_R6_SPARSE_LATTICE_3TO1_RESULTS.json, status ALL_EXACT_ASSERTIONS_PASSED. An independent JavaScript Number-in-safe-integer-range implementation recalculates all 309 differences and 189,726 algebraic intersection candidates and obtains the identical totals. No floating arithmetic is used for the mathematical counts (division is integer floor/ceiling on exact <=2^53 inputs).

The infinite lifting theorem has a symbolic constructive proof, not an exhaustive infinite computation. This p=32 count is a finite exhaustive arithmetic certificate for the declared set, with exact finite coverage as proved above. Code and JSON are supplied in the same research_notes/portable_direct directory. Frozen input, P000, ACTIVE residual-preserving viewpoint and project authority are unchanged.

## Next discriminating question

Generalize the lattice certificate to bounded k,l with de-duplication across coefficient ratios, then test whether combined sparse-lattice obstructions can eliminate a complete gcd family or yield a 19-bit collision-free candidate. Any total no-go must cover *every* admissible (q1,q2), not just these certificates. Independently test whether the exact p=32 observer condition admits a positive 19-bit pair. Current shared X6 ownership remains separate; this note neither creates a CLAIM nor promotes an auxiliary observer result to an X6 dynamics theorem.
